problem_statement: alexdeploy/developer-portfolio-v2 is a Nuxt 3 developer-portfolio (Sable Ortega, a creative front-end engineer) with a VS-Code-editor visual language, built statically with nuxt generate and served from .output/public across the home, about-me, projects, and contact-me routes. The portfolio needs a shared 'Project architecture' rail that summarises how the six shipped projects are organised (component stacks, live surfaces, coastal datasets, field companions) and that appears consistently on the home, projects, AND about-me routes so the 'read the architecture, then dive into a project' narrative holds across the site. The rail must lay out its four metric tiles responsively so the document never overflows horizontally on tablet or mobile, and it must match the site's dark VS-Code palette. On the projects page, the existing technology filter must expose a live 'Showing N of M' readout that updates on every filter click to reflect the current selection (e.g. 'Showing 2 of 6 · React' after clicking React).
required_content: A shared 'Project architecture' rail (a new components/ArchStrip.vue) renders on the home, projects AND about-me routes, summarising the six projects as four metric tiles (component stacks, live surfaces, coastal datasets, field companions).
The rail's tile row wraps responsively so the whole document never overflows horizontally on tablet or mobile (documentElement scrollWidth stays within the viewport, tolerance 24px).
The rail uses the site's dark VS-Code palette (deep-blue card, teal eyebrow, indigo metric numerals) so it matches the surrounding portfolio rather than introducing an off-brand card.

On the projects page, the technology filter exposes a live '#filter-readout' that updates on every filter click: after clicking React it reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · React', and it returns to 'Showing 6 of 6 · all' when no technology is selected.
The existing Nuxt routes, the VS-Code editor layout, the ProjectCard grid, the tech-filter checkbox behaviour, and the Sable Ortega persona all stay intact (no regressions).
design_constraints: Reuse the template's own local assets (public/icons/techs/*.svg tech icons) and the existing Nuxt VS-Code styling; introduce no external or remote media.
The shared rail must be a single component rendered from app.vue on the whitelisted routes so its cross-page presence is consistent; do not duplicate divergent copies per page.
Keep the rail's four tiles on a wrapping row (flex-wrap) with a fluid basis so tablet and mobile never overflow; do not pin the row to a fixed pixel width.
The projects filter readout must be a reactive/computed value bound to the live filter set, not a value snapshotted once at component setup.
state_constraints: The initial states (desktop, tablet, mobile) capture the home hero at the top of the page; the restyle must land the Sable Ortega name and role above the fold on desktop_initial.

The projects states capture the /projects route: desktop_projects and mobile_projects show the full six-card grid, desktop_projects_react_filter clicks the React checkbox to narrow the grid, desktop_projects_empty_filter clicks a technology with no project to show the empty state, and mobile_projects_filter_open shows the mobile filter sidebar.

change_completion: The 'Project architecture' rail renders on the home, projects, and about-me routes with its four metric tiles and grounded copy.
The projects filter readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · React' after the React filter is clicked, reflecting the live selection.
design_consistency: The rail matches the site's dark VS-Code palette (deep-blue card, teal eyebrow, indigo metrics) rather than an off-brand light card, matching the reference visually.
The rail reuses the template's own tech icons and the existing Nuxt layout, and the ProjectCard grid and tech-filter chrome stay intact.
responsive: The rail's tile row wraps on tablet and mobile so the document does not overflow horizontally beyond the 24px tolerance on mobile_initial.
The home hero, projects grid, and rail remain usable across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.
regression: The Sable Ortega hero name and role remain present so the persona and site chrome stay intact.
The tech-filter still narrows the ProjectCard grid and shows the 'No matching projects' empty state for a technology with no matches.

author_notes: L4-hardened restyle: the shared project-architecture rail is the vehicle for four orthogonal gates. D6 (no_horizontal_overflow) is measured on mobile_initial where the rail is present in all legs; D3 (visual_regression) compares the rail's home render against the reference; D2 (dom_assertions) checks the rail's cross-page presence on projects and about-me; D4 (interaction_assertions) checks the projects filter readout updates live after clicking React. The baseline reproduces the original layout defect (fixed-width non-wrapping row) so it fails D6/D3/D2 but not D4; the bad solution is a smart-wrong restyle that additionally swaps the palette and freezes the readout so it fails all four.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Nuxt 3 developer-portfolio with a centralised developer.json content model, a VS-Code editor layout, a multi-route structure (home / projects / about-me / contact-me), and a projects tech-filter — an ideal host for an L4 design-continuity task that adds a shared cross-page project-architecture rail (D2/D3/D6) and wires a live filter readout (D4).
